stories.title: Sources: Rams' Puka Nacua out 4-5 months after knee surgery, will miss playoffs
stories.summary: Puka Nacua's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be 4-5 months, sources told ESPN, meaning he will miss the playoffs.
stories.detail: Puka Nacua 's recovery time from his MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning the Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver will miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs. Sources told ESPN that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the surgery, which is expected to have him healthy for the 2027 season. Nacua's knee checked out clean aside from the MCL, according to a source. The operation was performed by team doctor Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN. Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing the MCL surgery Tuesday. McVay added that the possibility of Nacua returning for the postseason was a scenario that the Rams "haven't thought about." The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN on Friday. In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the knee injury, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the …

stories.title: 40-year-old Josh Johnson making historic Cardinals start not seen since Jim Thorpe
stories.summary: It is rarely a positive development for a team that it must start a fourth different quarterback in four weeks.
stories.detail: Josh Johnson Jim Thorpe It is rarely a positive development for a team that it must start a fourth different quarterback in four weeks. For the Cardinals, it is somewhat historic. The quarterback-desperate Cardinals will turn to the ageless but also aged Josh Johnson on Sunday in Kansas City, where the longtime backup will play a game at 40 years and 191 days old. Arizona Cardinals quarterback Josh Johnson leaves the field after an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams in Glendale, Ariz., Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/Ross D. Franklin According to Mark Dalton , the organization’s senior vice president of media relations, Johnson will become the second-oldest non-specialist to play in a game for the Cardinals. To find the oldest, go all the way to Jim Thorpe in 1928, when the legend was 41 years and 185 days old in a Thanksgiving Day game against the Bears (which did not go well, with the Chicago Cardinals losing 34-0). stories.title: Steelers need more from DK Metcalf, other highly paid players
stories.summary: Tight end Pat Freiermuth, linebacker Alex Highsmith and quarterback Aaron Rodgers also have not lived up to their contracts at times in 2026.
stories.detail: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-3 and still well positioned to make the NFL playoffs because of a favorable schedule. For that reason, the 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 15 was not a total disaster and could plausibly be written off as just a bad day against a red-hot offense led by leading MVP candidate Joe Burrow. At least that might be true if the team’s most highly paid players were producing at the levels they’re paid to. They decidedly are not, and until they are, then the Steelers still profile as an upper middle class AFC team capable of reaching the postseason, but probably not winning once they get there. Required reading: Steelers' veteran CB was torched by Joe Burrow in loss to Bengals: PFF grades Receiver DK Metcalf, who’s in Year 2 of a five-year, $150 million deal, is the chief offender. Through nine games, he’s on pace for the least productive season of his eight-year NFL career. It would break the lower threshold that he established last just year, his first in Pittsburgh, when he had 850 yards. Pro Football Focus data faults him for six drops, a figure that feels generous given how frequently he fails to come down with catchable balls from quarterback…

stories.title: Kicker Smyth elevated to Saints' playing roster
stories.summary: Kicker Charlie Smyth is elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise.
stories.detail: [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth has been elevated to the New Orleans Saints' playing roster and has signed a new deal with the NFL franchise. The former gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in Northern Ireland, has started the last two NFL games for the Saints after being promoted from the practice squad. The 25-year-old was handed a second opportunity to be the Saints' kicker after Dan Carlson, who started the season as first choice, was released at the start of November due to mixed form. Smyth helped the Saints to an overtime win over the Cleveland Browns on his return to the team and then kicked a late 55-yard field goal in the 20-17 defeat by the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. NFL rules state a player from a practice squad cannot be used more than three times in a season, and Smyth has been rewarded for his impressive return. He made his NFL debut for New Orleans last November but was released by the franchise in August. Smyth was retained on their practice squad due to having an exemption as he came through the NFL's international player pathway. His first game since signing his new deal is at the Chicago Bears on Sunday at 18:00 GMT. NFL fixtures and results Get American Fo…

stories.title: 76ers survive in clutch again despite Herro's 50: 'Got to finish better'
stories.summary: The 76ers survived 50 points from Tyler Herro, nearly blowing a 10-point lead late, before once again coming out on top in the clutch.
stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- In a season full of wins that keep this fanbase stressed until the final buzzer, the Philadelphia 76ers ' 132-129 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday followed suit. The Sixers survived a career-high 50 points from Bucks guard Tyler Herro , who nailed a contested fadeaway 3-pointer at the end of regulation that would have tied the score, but an official review determined Herro released the ball just after time expired. After the game, Sixers center Joel Embiid , who led the team with 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists, praised Herro as "a top five player in the league." The win moved the Sixers to 14-3, which is tied for the NBA's best record and their best 17-game start since 2000-01, when they last reached the NBA Finals. And yet, much of the conversation after their most recent victory centered on how they're winning games. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better," said LeBron James , who finished with 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. "But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for their minutes. It's about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn'…

And his performance showed why he’s deserving of more playing opportunities moving forward.
